observations: Earlier left lifting tilted the pot (9,10).
Right lift tests missed; subsequent contact displaced the pot (15,19–21).
The pot rotated during closure and repositioning (33).
Right forward targets repeatedly failed planning (34–36).
Partial closure near 11 cm was transient, not proof of capture (37,38).
The left wrist rose 4.78 cm while the pot remained on the table; the right lift failed planning (38).
Both grippers finished fully closed at 4.9 cm separation (38).
hypotheses: The right arm's current configuration may severely restrict reachable nearby targets.
astra_final_memory.summary: Attempt 1 failed to secure both handles. Pot remains on the table after the lift test (38). Do not interpret transient 11 cm separation during closure as a grasp: both fingers subsequently reached 4.9 cm. Right forward and upward motions repeatedly failed (34–36,38). A fresh attempt should establish accessible bilateral approach poses and verify completed closure before lifting.

observations: The measured empty fully closed finger separation is 4.9 cm (47,50).
The pot visibly rose approximately 8 cm while right separation remained 10.99 cm and left separation was 4.9 cm; bilateral capture was not established (47–48).
Both additional 5 cm upward plans failed (49).
Moving upward and backward caused right separation to fall to 4.9 cm, with 2.02 cm position error and 13.9 degrees orientation error; the pot disappeared from view (50).
Both arms successfully withdrew and opened, but the pot remained absent from all camera views after 498 simulation steps; completion remained false (51).
hypotheses: The pot may have been displaced outside the visible workspace.
Restricted reach and asymmetric support may have contributed to losing the pot.
astra_final_memory.summary: Attempt ended without completion after losing the pot. Right-only support apparently lifted it approximately 8 cm (47–48), but left fingers were fully closed at the empty 4.9 cm separation. Further upward plans failed (49); moving upward and backward lost right capture and the pot disappeared (50). Opening and withdrawing both arms did not reveal it after settling (51). A fresh attempt should verify settled bilateral capture before lifting and avoid treating unilateral suspension as a secure two-arm grasp.
